summary: Bridge call after HelioHealth reported multiple latency regressions during peak traffic last week. Discussed suspected root causes (KV cache thrash + aggressive autoscaler behavior), immediate mitigations (increase cooldowns, pre-warm KV cache, tweak fallback routing), longer-term hardenings (sticky prefixes, tracing hooks, canary rollout plan, improved observability for per-token latency). Agreed on concrete next steps and a staging validation run.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortega (Redwood AE), Sanjay Rao (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Redwood CSM); Maria Lopez (HelioHealth CTO), Evan Clarke (HelioHealth SRE), Priya Nair (Head of AI), Jordan Kim (Infra Eng)

Auto-summary: HelioHealth hit a latency regression under peak which appears correlated with node churn and KV cache miss storms; Redwood and customer to run staging perf, apply autoscaler cooldown, and instrument deeper traces.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood): okay hey everyone thanks for carving time, we know this has been pretty disruptive, so we'll get into the timeline and what we've validated so far. I'm Jamie, AE on the account. Sanjay will lead the root cause and next steps.
[00:18] Maria (HelioHealth): thanks, yeah appreciate it. We had two severe spikes last tuesday and thursday during our billing batch windows, p95 jumped to 3.2s from a baseline of 220ms, and a few hundred requests timed out.
[00:34] Evan (HelioHealth): and importantly it wasn't steady, it was like 10 minutes of very bad latency, then a drop, then hit again. Our alerting kicked off but we were scrambling to find the trigger.
[00:48] Sanjay (Redwood): right, we pulled the initial traces. There are a couple of overlapping signals: increased pod/node churn in the dedicated pool and a large number of KV cache evictions around the same time. When the KV cache misses spike, the per-token compute increases and the apparent latency balloons.
[01:05] Priya (HelioHealth): when you say node churn do you mean autoscaler is bringing down nodes mid-window? We thought we had reserved capacity for those peaks.
[01:14] Jamie (Redwood): this is the odd part — Dedicated commit is in place, but our autoscaler settings allowed some spill to burst nodes for headroom; during the burst the cooldowns and pre-warm weren't tuned to your traffic signature so the new nodes started cold, leading to cache misses.
[01:28] Jordan (HelioHealth): hmm we did see GPUs spin up and then a few evictions on the cache, the cache size looked to be consistent but the hot prefixes seemed to be purged.
[01:40] Sanjay (Redwood): exactly — and one more complication: an internal scheduling bug caused rebalancing to happen more aggressively under certain multi-tenant fragmentation scenarios, so the combination is: aggressive rebalancing + cooldown too short + cold node pre-warm mismatch = KV cache thrash.
[01:58] Maria (HelioHealth): is that a Redwood runtime bug or a config mismatch on our side? we need to be clear for procurement and legal.
[02:07] Sanjay (Redwood): preliminary root cause is configuration/tuning + a scheduler edge case. We take ownership for the scheduler fix and the patch to the cooldown heuristics; we'll propose a config baseline you can pin.
[02:18] Evan (HelioHealth): and does this affect our data residency or logs? we need to know if any payloads were routed outside the VPC during those events.
[02:27] Jamie (Redwood): from initial checks, all requests remained in the configured region. We'll include the routing and audit logs in the debug bundle. No evidence of off-VPC egress.
[02:36] Priya (HelioHealth): ok good, but we still need the end-to-end trace showing which nodes handled which requests. That will help us validate.
[02:44] Sanjay (Redwood): we will produce per-token latency traces and node assignment maps. expect those in the debug bundle.
[02:51] Maria (HelioHealth): i'd like to go over short-term mitigations first — what can we do in the next 48-72 hours to prevent recurrence?
[02:59] Jamie (Redwood): short term: 1) increase autoscaler cooldowns to avoid rapid churn, 2) force pre-warm on new nodes for pinned models, 3) adjust KV cache eviction thresholds to favor longer-lived prefixes, 4) implement a temporary routing policy to avoid falling back to the smaller quantized model unless absolutely necessary.
[03:18] Evan (HelioHealth): how invasive is pre-warm? will it cost a bunch of extra tokens or cause cold billing anomalies?
[03:27] Sanjay (Redwood): pre-warm is a small warmup batch against pinned prefixes; it's modest cost but cheaper than timeouts and SLO violations. We'll size it conservatively.
[03:36] Jordan (HelioHealth): and the fallback routing change — we saw some requests routed to the q4-quant variant which had higher per-token latencies in our traces?
[03:45] Sanjay (Redwood): yep, in your workload the quant path actually increased overall tail latency because it introduced extra CPU-to-GPU transfers in the current config. So temporary suppression of that fallback makes sense until we retune the quant path.
[03:58] Maria (HelioHealth): ok, long term what does a hardened setup look like? we need design for SLAs and for the SOC2 auditors.
[04:07] Jamie (Redwood): long term: sticky prefix caching for hot models, improved per-request tracing hooks, a canary rollout and routing policy that avoids cross-variant fallbacks during spikes, autoscaler policy changes to prefer burst capacity over immediate teardown, and stronger observability (per-token cost, per-route p50/p95/p99). We'll supply a template config and a runbook.
[04:27] Priya (HelioHealth): can you propose a canary plan that will let us validate without risking production? we'd like to see a plan that uses a subset of traffic and a staged ramp to 10/30/100%.
[04:38] Sanjay (Redwood): yes, we recommend progressive traffic shifting: start at 1% steady traffic with tracing, then 10% for 30 minutes with synthetic load, then 30% for 2 hours. We'll provide metrics to watch (cache hit rate, node churn, per-token latency).
[04:57] Evan (HelioHealth): about observability, the tracing we saw was aggregated and we couldn't easily reconstruct the timeline - can you add per-request node id and per-token latency in traces?
[05:10] Sanjay (Redwood): that's on the list. We'll expose node_id and kv_cache_hit flags in the trace. We'll also add a KV cache eviction event stream to the console for your team.
[05:22] Maria (HelioHealth): legal will ask about mitigation credit and SLA breach. what's Redwood's stance?
[05:30] Jamie (Redwood): we'll follow the contract — but independent of that, we'll propose a goodwill credit for the customer-impacting windows and speed-prioritize the patch. We'll include proposed credit in the follow-up.
[05:42] Jordan (HelioHealth): quick question — during the churn did any requests get retried automatically by your client? we saw some duplicated logs on our side.
[05:51] Sanjay (Redwood): some SDK retries happened; we can provide guidance to tune client-side retry/backoff and also roll an automatic jittered backoff at the edge to avoid thundering herds.
[06:05] Maria (HelioHealth): good. Can we talk about compliance risks — any logs containing PHI or payloads that could be sensitive?
[06:13] Jamie (Redwood): you are under Private deployment with redaction and retention policies set; we'll redact payloads before sending debug artifacts and only share pointers to audit logs per your KMS policies. We'll also include the KMS key IDs used for encryption.
[06:25] Priya (HelioHealth): going deeper on root cause — is the scheduler edge case something that's reproducible in staging?
[06:34] Sanjay (Redwood): we've recreated a similar scenario in a small repro: when multi-model fragmentation hits certain packing heuristics while autoscaler triggers simultaneous scale-ins and scale-outs, it can cause suboptimal placement. We'll include the repro steps in the ticket.
[06:49] Evan (HelioHealth): what's the risk of the fix breaking other customers' placement behavior? we don't want a global change that regresses others.
[06:58] Sanjay (Redwood): valid concern. We'll ship the scheduler fix behind a feature flag and gate it to your tenant and a couple internal test tenants. We'll also run rollout canaries.
[07:10] Maria (HelioHealth): timeline for the patch?
[07:13] Jamie (Redwood): initial patch to cooldown heuristics and pre-warm toggle into staging within 48 hours; scheduler fix behind flag in two weeks, then a controlled rollout.
[07:23] Priya (HelioHealth): for the canary and load test, we want to run our real prompts (PII redacted) through your staging cluster. Can you support that?
[07:32] Sanjay (Redwood): yes, we propose a staging run next week; we'll need a dataset and a time window. We'll also provide a runbook and guardrails.
[07:42] Jordan (HelioHealth): and to validate we want to see p99 token latency, cache hit curves, and node churn timeline.
[07:50] Sanjay (Redwood): will include those metrics and an annotation timeline so you can map events.
[07:57] Maria (HelioHealth): any immediate configuration we should flip now?
[08:01] Jamie (Redwood): increase autoscaler scale-in cooldown to 15 minutes, enable pre-warm for the two highest-volume models, temporarily disable quant fallback for your tenant. We'll apply to staging first then to prod on a maintenance window you approve.
[08:19] Evan (HelioHealth): please also include a flag to revert quickly if we see regressions.
[08:24] Sanjay (Redwood): acknowledged; revert flag and playbook will be included.
[08:29] Maria (HelioHealth): okay, that covers fixes. let's capture deliverables.
[08:34] Jamie (Redwood): deliverables: debug bundle with traces and audit logs; staging run with Helio vectors; autoscaler cooldown patch in staging; pre-warm toggle; proposed credit statement.
[08:46] Lena (Redwood): i'll own scheduling the follow-up and wrangling the security docs. expect invites.
[08:51] Maria (HelioHealth): thanks. can you set the follow-up for early next week and include our legal and procurement? they'll want the evidence.
[08:58] Jamie (Redwood): will do.
[09:02] Priya (HelioHealth): one more ask — could Redwood share recommended quantization profile changes that have been validated on similar workloads?
[09:10] Sanjay (Redwood): yes, we'll include quant profiles and perf numbers; caveat that quant tuning is model and workload dependent.
[09:19] Maria (HelioHealth): ok any final questions?
[09:24] Jordan (HelioHealth): none from infra.
[09:26] Evan (HelioHealth): none here.
[09:28] Jamie (Redwood): thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the debug artifacts by 2026-12-24 and schedule the staging run for the week of 2027-01-04.
[09:39] Meeting end.
